catalog.summary: Text export of the 'GSMG Puzzle Solvers' Telegram group, 13,215 lines; mostly 2019-04-20..2020-10-15 with a few later (2021-2026) messages interleaved out of order. Includes about 160 posts by the group admin JrK, who speaks for the puzzle team (typo fix, hash for stage 1, the 2020 hint, prize-halving remarks).

Truncated enumeration (4,793 lines) of A1Z26 segmentations of one word-spaced digit string. The base form uses only A-I (=1-9); each variant merges digit pairs into letters J-Z (e.g. AE->O, AF->P, BE->Y, AC->M). No readable line seen.
Comma-separated RGBA pixel dump of the first puzzle image ('follow the white rabbit'), truncated at 400 kB. Values seen are only 255, 0, 72, 63, 204 and 242 (palette image).

Per-frame MP3 header and side-info dump (46 frames, MPEG-1 Layer III, 320 kbps, 44.1 kHz, joint stereo) of an audio file, probably the puzzle's song. The copyright, original and private bits are 0 in every frame.

A 62,329-byte JPEG (JFIF with an ICC profile) embedded as an Arduino PROGMEM C byte array. It ends in a long run of 0x00 before 0x3f,0xff,0xd9. The file name is a ms timestamp, 2025-07-13. The image itself is unknown.

Scored output (5,000 rows) of a grid-traversal bit-reading search: path (spiral/snake/diagonal/onion...), width 7/8, offset, bit-reverse and 5-bit mapping. Top row 'gsmg.io/theseedisplantet' (Spiral_CCW_TL, w=8) is a 1-char-off rediscovery of the known Phase 1 answer; the rest is noise.

OCR/markdown text of the Time-Life book 'Mysteries of the Unknown: Cosmic Duality' (yin-yang, Zoroaster, Manicheanism, The Exorcist...). This is the reference behind the 'cosmic duality' phase. No puzzle annotations.
catalog.author: Editors of Time-Life Books (published book)

leads.claim: Admin, 2020-02-22 20:30, replying to a user describing a 3D game ('parcel', 'interactive mode', 'pushed the red button and I was locked into a building'): 'Only -41,-17 matters'. Read this as a single game-world parcel coordinate, most likely Decentraland, that is the side-quest location. Related admin posts: 2019-09-26 'There may indeed a piece be found outside the main puzzle.'; 2020-02-25 'Not sponsored, just see it as a side quest'.
exact_strings: Only -41,-17 matters
There may indeed a piece be found outside the main puzzle.
leads.self_verifying: Only by inspecting the external parcel's scene content (an external site, not visited here). Any string found there would still need an AES/URL test against puzzle data.

leads.claim: Admin, 2020-03-25, was asked whether the PK is in the last cipher of the decoded 3.2 and answered: 'There must at least be something hidden in there.' Also 'Answering that would be too much of a hint' to whether the PK is split into pieces, and 2020-02-25 '3.2 is a thing btw' / 'most see 3.2 as the last part.' This supports the c37 'inner blob first' view: the last Phase 3.2 blob contains something.
exact_strings: There must at least be something hidden in there.
3.2 is a thing btw
Don't know but most see 3.2 as the last part.
leads.self_verifying: Any password candidate for the inner 3.2 blob verifies itself by openssl padding plus readable plaintext. The hint gives no candidate.

leads.claim: Admin 'door' remarks about the first piece. 2020-05-11: 'who knows what you'll find after opening the 2nd door. The price is in half, but what does it mean'. 2020-05-21: 'answer is there', then to 'Do you mean the answer to another door from the 1st piece?' replied 'First or zero'. 2020-08-02: 'Really nobody managed to find the extra door'. 2020-08-12: 'Indeed remarkable with the hints stating the path pretty obvious...'. 'First or zero' may mean indexing from 0 or the first piece itself.

answer is there
First or zero
Really nobody managed to find the extra door
leads.self_verifying: A second door would show up as a non-404 gsmg.io path or an openssl-padding-valid decrypt

Although I can say that one team managed to find something... something others haven't yet found'. 2020-08-12: 'There's 1 club that passed but they are stuck in the next phase.' 2020-10-01: 'number 2 has made it to the next stage.' So at least two teams privately passed a stage beyond the public frontier (probably the 2020-hint door or SalPhaseIon).

The admin said the mistake needs 1 extra character added between the 3 answers. 2020-04-08 he restates it the other way round: 'The biggest blunder ... was givetit instead of giveit'. Also: 'No hints after stage 2 (except the 't' ...)' and 'errors and typos are mostly not intended'.

leads.claim: The admin gave a SHA-256 hash (2019-04-22) so players could test stage-1 password candidates offline instead of against the website.

User 139037664, 2020-10-15: 'The last part of gsmg puzzle is actuely a plaint text with out cbc cipher', plus 'decrease size of string... Base64 to ascii'. Quoted blob (first 2 lines): U2FsdGVkX1+0Wl49gnWTyiim... The 'U2FsdGVkX1' prefix decodes to 'Salted__', so it is an openssl salted ciphertext, not plaintext; the claim is self-refuting. The same blob appears elsewhere in the log (lines ~10899, 13202).
exact_strings: U2FsdGVkX1+0Wl49gnWTyiimluu7V3+vl7st0gUt9sWDzNLxDmlPMsDSiuW2a46z
gKlIi8aaqY5gpJPPEzW1n9n3/26qs4zstWtPKF8Zs/BTNN4IiEh4qu18mdC0NAv4
leads.self_verifying: base64 header 'Salted__' + 8-byte salt proves it is encrypted. Check which known blob it is (likely a 3.2/SalPhaseIon blob).
